//: COFFEE CONTEXT. Read `attack/README.md` §4 before adding to `adjacentDomains`. The sentences in that field are NOT generated — they are human work, transcribed verbatim from the decaf review's measured findings (standards/coffee/v1.0/vocabulary/decaf-method.json, review.adversarial_findings + insufficient_evidence). The generator replays them; it did not and could not derive them. Anything the generator replays is coverage the HUMAN supplied, and the coverage report must not be read as though the machine found it.

adjacentDomains.why: On virtually every specialty coffee page `Process` names the post-harvest treatment — washed, natural, honey — and says nothing about decaffeination. A check keyed on that word reads a drying method as a solvent disclosure, which the decaf review recorded as the most dangerous near-miss in the whole standard.
sentences: Process: Washed, 1750 masl, Caturra and Castillo.
A natural process Ethiopian with big fruit and a syrupy body.

adjacentDomains.domain: carbonic maceration, a post-harvest fermentation style
adjacentDomains.why: Carbonic maceration natural is a widespread post-harvest technique that shares its name with a registered CO2 decaffeination mark. Two unrelated processes, one string — the decaf review's strongest single finding.
sentences: Ethiopia Guji, carbonic natural, 48-hour anaerobic fermentation.

adjacentDomains.why: Ethyl acetate is a named sensory defect on the trade's own cupping form as well as a decaffeination solvent. The same compound, and the opposite claim about the coffee.
sentences: Overripe fruit and ethyl acetate notes indicate over-fermentation.
Clean cup, balanced acidity, syrupy body and a long finish.

adjacentDomains.why: Emissions copy is near-universal on coffee product pages and has nothing to do with caffeine removal. This is why `carbon dioxide process` could not be a term and was replaced by `carbon dioxide decaffeination`.
sentences: We have cut our carbon dioxide process emissions by 40% since 2020.

adjacentDomains.why: Nitro and sparkling coffee are mainstream roaster lines, and liquid carbon dioxide is ordinary dispense and modified-atmosphere vocabulary there.
sentences: Nitro cold brew is charged with liquid CO2 and nitrogen for texture.
Each bag is flushed with liquid CO2 before sealing.

adjacentDomains.why: Supercritical carbon dioxide is the dominant extraction method for hops, hemp and flavour extracts, so a roaster with a syrup or extract line writes it about a different product.
sentences: Our botanical extracts are made with supercritical CO2 extraction.
The lion's mane extract in this blend is produced with supercritical CO2.

adjacentDomains.why: Cane-sugar co-fermentation is a current and fast-growing Colombian post-harvest technique written in exactly this form, and it happens at the mill rather than at a decaffeination plant.
sentences: The sugarcane process at the mill adds cane molasses during fermentation.

adjacentDomains.why: Sugarcane is one of the commonest flavour descriptors in coffee copy as well as the name of an ethyl-acetate process. The bare word is a flavour claim far more often than a process claim.
sentences: Notes of sugarcane, cocoa nib and toasted almond.

adjacentDomains.domain: a rival trade name that contains the same substring
adjacentDomains.why: A CO2 extraction is marketed under a water-sounding trade name, so any matcher treating the literal substring `water process` as evidence of a water method classifies a carbon-dioxide process as a water one. This is the measured reason `water process` can never be a supporting term.
sentences: Decaffeinated by the Sparkling Water Process for a sweeter cup.
Swiss water is the softest water in Europe.
